brief: A Zero Hedge repost of the chart pack Goldman's Johannes Duttenhoefer says drew attention from Goldman traders this week. It compiles charts with one-line captions and does not argue a thesis. Positioning: the US Fundamental Long/Short ratio and US net leverage both sit in the 4th percentile on a 1yr horizon on Prime data as of 5-Sep-26, gold speculative positioning reversed sharply through late August, and the Tech Long/Short Momentum pair is down about 50% from late-June highs. Europe versus US: capex drags US free cash flow yields against Europe, US concentration stays higher, equity flows have avoided Europe since 2020, and EUR investment grade and bond yields now compete with European dividends. Automation: robot shipment forecasts quadruple, robotics VC funding accelerates, robot costs are set to fall 7% a year, and AI task-completion horizons double every 7 months, shown against aging developed-market populations and high labor costs. Also carried: French yields above Greece on fiscal concerns, 2025 effective tax rates pressuring corporate profits, DDR5 spot prices rising, negative hyperscaler free cash flow through 2027 before a 2028 rebound, and a rebound in private credit flows.
